titel: A Wagging Tail Doesn't Mean Happy

beats.say: Why does a wagging tail... *not* mean your dog is happy?
Rudi doesn't know that. He sees a wag... and goes in for a *hug.*
The dog growls. So Rudi builds a *wag-o-meter.* It says: super happy. The dog still *growls.*
The meter didn't help, so now Rudi says hi... in a full suit of *armor.*
Here's the truth. A wag just means your dog feels *something.* Happy, nervous... or *angry.*
Scientists in Italy found: dogs wag more to the *right* when relaxed... and to the *left* when stressed.
And a stiff tail, held *high*, wagging fast? That can mean: *back off.*
Here's what to do: look at the *whole* dog. Loose, wiggly body? Go ahead.
Stiff and frozen? Give it *space.* And if your friends ever ask you...
